macros.name: aligned
macros.doc: To align the left edge of the box containing the object to the reference point, specify \aligned{left}.

macros.name: area
macros.doc: The set of consecutive lines in relation to which a text object is to be positioned is delimited by a pair of commands: \area \endarea (or \Area \endArea); you may also place the set within the area (or Area) environment.

macros.name: Capita
macros.doc: \Capita is a (very slightly) modified version of \setmarks, with the same syntax; it is used exactly where \setmarks would normally occur.

macros.name: commissura
macros.doc: If you judge that it would be better to split the paragraph at an earlier point than the one selected by the software, you can force the split by inserting the \commissura command at that point.

macros.name: Delimiter
macros.doc: A delimiter is generated by the \Delimiter command; the command argument is the TeX control sequence for the delimiter, which may be one of the basic set of 22 listed on page 146 of The TEXbook or one of the special delimiters listed on page 150.

macros.name: DriveOut
macros.doc: The normal form of the \DriveOut command is meant to be used at the start of a TeX group and it affects all text within the group; the * -form applies to the text that follows, up to the end of the paragraph.

macros.name: DropCap
macros.doc: For large dropped capitals, as used in traditional French typography, you can use the \DropCap command, which is the functional equivalent of the \lettrine command in the very versatile package of the same name by Daniel Flipo (tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/lettrine).

macros.doc: With both the \headline and the \contents commands you can specify an argument providing the information to be passed to the respective destination instead of the default information.

macros.name: HouseStyle
macros.doc: The command \HouseStyle{<style>} looks for a file named <style>.hs and reads it in.

macros.doc: The \multiples (or \multiple) command identifies a special type of subclass, whose objects consist of a piece of text repeated as many times as necessary to fill a given width.

macros.name: NumberRange
macros.doc: The command \NumberRange takes three arguments: the first two are the lower and upper limits of the range, the third, which must be the name of a LaTeX counter, is set by the command to the value to be used for the upper limit.

macros.name: OldStyleNums
macros.doc: The \OldStyleNums command has the same effect as the standard LaTeX command \oldstylenums, except that it leaves any non-digit characters in the argument unaltered.

macros.name: ordinal
macros.doc: The command \ordinal {<number >} places the representation of the ordinal number corresponding to <number > (which must be ≤ 25) in the control sequence \theordinal.

macros.name: pagewise
macros.doc: The \pagewise command causes the counter associated with a line number to be reset to 1 at the start of each page.

macros.name: rangedleft
macros.doc: \rangedleft \rangedright all lines are ranged left and right, respectively.

macros.name: rangedright
macros.doc: \rangedleft \rangedright all lines are ranged left and right, respectively.

macros.name: RelSize
macros.doc: \RelSize{n} changes the font size, relative to the current size, by n steps (up or down depending on the sign of n) in the standard LaTeX range that extends from \tiny to \Huge; if the size requested is too large or too small, \Huge or \tiny, respectively, is used.

macros.name: RomanNumeral
macros.doc: The \RomanNumeral{<number >} and \ROMANnumeral{<number >} commands yield the numeral in, respectively, small and full capitals.

macros.doc: The \Rule command generates a horizontal rule with a width equal to the value of \hsize for the text in which it appears, taking \leftskip and \rightskip into account.

macros.name: textus
macros.doc: Any text that appears within Versus or Prosa and is not the argument of a subclass command is treated as an object of the default \textus subclass.

macros.name: TextWidth
macros.doc: The \TextWidth command sets, in addition to \textwidth, two other LaTeX parameters: \linewidth and \columnwidth.

macros.name: unhyphenated
